# Example 1 (Basic) {.unnumbered}

In this example, we'll use a simple two-rack compartment configuration and a single vehicle to illustrate the workings.

## Data 

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

data <- read.csv('../../../sample_data/publist_orders.csv')[1:9, ] 

number_pubs <- nrow(data)
```

The data used in this example is a list of `r number_pubs` pubs in Dublin, Ireland with their associated X and Y coordinates, pickup and dropoff times, and quantities (amount added to a vehicle at each location). There are 8 pickups and 8 dropoffs.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: false

if(!("pacman" %in% rownames(installed.packages()))){
  install.packages("pacman")
}

library(pacman)
p_load(tidyverse)
p_load(DT)
p_load(dplyr)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: true

data <- data %>% mutate(across(2:3, ~ format(round(.x, digits=5), nsmall = 5))) 

datatable(data, colnames = c("Pub Name (id)",
                           "X-Coordinate (X)",
                           "Y-Coordinate (Y)",
                           "Pickup Time (pickupTime)",
                           "Dropoff Time (dropoffTime)",
                           "Quantity (quantity)")
                           , options = list(dom = 't', scrollY = "200px", pageLength=nrow(data), columnDefs = list(list(className = 'dt-right', targets = 2:6))))
```

## Running the example

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
library(iceR)

source('ivr8-model-helper.R')
```

Execute the example as follows:

### 1. Create an apiHelper object with the model type you'd like to solve

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
api <- new("apiHelper", modelType = 'ivr8-yni1c9k2swof', configFile = '../../../config.json')
```

### 2. Create the model and add some data to it

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

# Create the model
sr <- new (IVR8.SolveRequest)
sr$model <- new (IVR8.Model)

# Load the data (we're going to use location 1 as the depot and locations 2 to 9 as the stops)
data <- read.csv('../../../sample_data/publist_orders.csv')[1:9, ]

# View the loaded data (if desired)
ggplot() + geom_point(data = data, aes(x = X, y = Y)) + theme_bw()
```
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false

# Configure the model and add the data to it (See ivr8-model-helper.R for details around some of the methods used below)

# (a) Dimensions, Locations, Jobs, Vehicles, Vehicle Classes and Vehicle Cost Classes (see the IVR7 example for more details around this)
sr$model$dimensions <- make_distance_time_cap_dims()
sr$model$locations <- make_locations(data)
sr$model$jobs <- make_job_time_cap(data, src = rep(1, nrow(data) - 1), dest = 2:nrow(data))
sr$model$vehicleCostClasses <- make_vcc_simple('vcc1', 1000, 0.01, 0.01, 0.01, 1, 3)
sr$model$vehicleClasses <- make_vc_simple('vc1', 1, 1, 1, 1)
sr$model$vehicles <- make_vehicle_cap("vehicle_1", 'vc1', 'vcc1',
                                   2000, # the vehicle capacity
                                   data$id[1], # start location
                                   data$id[1], # end location
                                   7*60,  # 7 AM
                                   18*60) # 6 PM

# (b) Compartments and Compartment Sets
# We're going to add some constraints around the compartments on the vehicle.

data$quantity %>% sum # 1800
# The sum of quantities at each stop (1800) is less than the total capacity of the vehicle (2000), but does it meet our compartment contraints?

# We're going to assume that we have a vehicle which is layed out as follows:
#  Top Rack    [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]  100kg per "compartment"  c1, c2, c3, c4
#  Lower Rack  [ ] [ ] [ ] [ ]  400kg per "compartment"  c5, c6, c7, c8
100*4 + 400*4 # adds up to the 2 tonne total limit on a vehicle (if every compartment could be filled to max)

# Compartments can be defined separately to compartments sets.
# You can use any combination of compartment definitions in a compartment set 
# (to define a collection against which constraint checks are performed)
sr$model$compartments <- list()
for(i in 1:8){
  comp <- new (IVR8.Compartment)
  comp$id <- paste0("c", i)
  comp$capacities <- new (IVR8.Compartment.Capacity)
  comp$capacities[[1]]$dimensionId <- "capacity"
  if(i <= 4){
    comp$capacities[[1]]$capacity <- 100 # top rack
  }else{
    comp$capacities[[1]]$capacity <- 400 # bottom rack
  }
  sr$model$compartments  <- append(sr$model$compartments, comp)
}

# Now we can define a compartment set (a container for the individual compartments)
# which is attached to a vehicle.
cset <- new (IVR8.CompartmentSet)
cset$id <- 'double-decker'
cset$compartmentIds <- paste0('c', 1:8) # indicates that this compartment set has c1:c8 available
sr$model$compartmentSets <- cset # add it to the model

# Then we assign the "double-decker" compartment set to the vehicle class.
# NOTE: We could have added it to each vehicle but this is easier.
sr$model$vehicleClasses[[1]]$compartmentSetId <- 'double-decker'

# Set the other relevant information
sr$solveType <- 0 # 0 for optimise, 1 for evaluate, 2 for reoptimise

# View the model in plain-text format (string or JSON)
sr$model$toString() %>% cat
sr$model$toJSON() %>% cat
```

### 3. Submit the model to the API

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
requestID <- api %>% postSolveRequest(sr)  
```

### 4. Retrieve the model response

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
resp <- api %>% getResponse(requestID)
```

### 5. Look at the result

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false

# Get the solve time
solveTime <- api %>% getSolveTime(requestID)
```

Solve time: `r solveTime`

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

resp$objective

# Tabulate the data in native-R format
tab <- resp %>% tabulate(sr)
tab$nodes %>% select(taskId, compartmentId, jobId)
tab$edges %>% head # just inspect the head of the output

# View the produced summary
tab$compartmentSummary

# Each "allocated" is when a task is executed (either a pickup or a dropoff). 
# The capacity of each compartment is listed at the top under "capacity".
# Each stop shows where the volume is added and we can see that only one change is made at each node.
# This is because the task is assigned to a compartment. At no point is the total volume allocated
# to a compartment more than the capacity of the compartment. There are 16 allocations here because there
# are 8 jobs, i.e. 8 pickups, 8 dropoffs. So after each pickup we can see the state of the load on
# the vehicle. Its maximum weight is at stop 8 => 1800 units.

# Plot the data (ggplot or leaflet)
resp %>% plotResponse(sr) # ggplot                       
resp %>% plotResponseLeaflet(sr) # leaflet (if it's mappable)
```

## Looking at an infeasible example

Here we will use the model from the above example, but clear the compartments and create a new list with slightly reduced capacity for the bottom rack compartments.

### 1. Update the model

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false

sr$model$compartments <- list()
for(i in 1:8){
  comp <- new (IVR8.Compartment)
  comp$id <- paste0("c", i)
  comp$capacities <- new (IVR8.Compartment.Capacity)
  comp$capacities[[1]]$dimensionId <- "capacity"
  if(i <= 4){
    comp$capacities[[1]]$capacity <- 150 # top rack
  }else{
    comp$capacities[[1]]$capacity <- 350 # bottom rack is at 350 - this is less than the biggest order
  }
  sr$model$compartments  <- append(sr$model$compartments, comp)
}
```

### 2. Submit the model to the API

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
requestID <- api %>% postSolveRequest(sr)  
```

### 3. Retrieve the model response

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false
resp <- api %>% getResponse(requestID)
```

### 4. Look at the result

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: false

# Get the solve time
solveTime <- api %>% getSolveTime(requestID)
```

Solve time: `r solveTime`

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

resp$objective

# Tabulate the data in native-R format
tab <- resp %>% tabulate(sr)
tab$nodes %>% select(taskId, compartmentId, jobId)
tab$edges %>% head # just inspect the head of the output

# View the produced summary and the infeasibilities
tab$compartmentSummary
tab$infeasibilities

# The API tells us that no feasible compartment assignment exists for this
# particular set of tasks as well as the constraining dimension (capacity).
# The limit and values are negative here indicating that the values aren't relevant.
# If you're looking for a more informative error message, use the evaluate endpoint which
# can identify for a proposed sequence where things went wrong (or whether any feasible sub-set exists).

# Plot the data (ggplot or leaflet)
resp %>% plotResponse(sr) # ggplot                       
resp %>% plotResponseLeaflet(sr) # leaflet (if it's mappable)
```
